items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1967-02-09
items.q: Benny Goodman's got a lot of things from Jimmy Noon, a lot of guys.

ctx.x: acquaintance from him. Would you say he was a real original?

I should say he was an original. Jimmy Noon was a great musician. And sure, he had his own sound. Because we copied a lot. Benny Goodman's got a lot of things from Jimmy Noon, a lot of guys. The only guy that played different from all of us, I'll be truthful, was Johnny Dodds. He had something different from all of them. I don't think he's taken any lessons. He learned in another way, but it was so beautiful. This guy played a lot of horn, man. He had his own sound, his own fingering and all. I wonder how he did…
Did you ever hear the original King Oliver Creole jazz band in about 22, 23, with Johnny Dodds and Dewdry at the Lincoln Gardens?

items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1972-06-26
items.q: Benny Goodman, he played nice, but he was a mechanical to me.

ctx.x: To get back to the early days, did you watch the other clarinet players carefully? Did you watch them to figure out anything?

Yes, you sure you got ears. I tell you, when I was coming up, I admired Artie Shaw was my favorite clarinet player. Benny Goodman, he played nice, but he was a mechanical to me. I didn't copy him, but I knew what they were making. But Artie Shaw had something else. He had a beautiful sound. He was a great musician. And this man was something else. I liked his band, Artie Shaw, in the third. You had another one you had. You had a lot of clarinet players. But it was all imitating Benny. And that was a little, Benny…
